recipes.name: Easy Money Breakfast Burritos
ingredients_raw: 1 (4 ounce) can diced green chilies, drained
0.75 cup process cheese food (such as Velveeta®), divided

steps.text: Place the pork sausage and onion into a skillet over medium heat, and cook until the sausage is browned, about 10 minutes. Break the meat apart into crumbles as it cooks. Drain the excess grease.

In a separate skillet over medium heat, melt the butter until the foam subsides, and cook and stir the beaten eggs with the chilies until softly scrambled but not wet, about 3 minutes. Transfer the scrambled eggs into a large bowl, and stir in the cooked sausage mixture.

Place a tortilla onto a microwave-safe plate, and cook in the microwave on High setting for 10 to 20 seconds. The tortilla should be warm and pliable. Spoon about 1/2 cup of the sausage and egg mixture in a line down the the tortilla, slightly off center. Top with about 1 tablespoon of shredded cheese, and 1 tablespoon of salsa. Fold 2 opposite ends of the tortilla over the filling. Press the 2 ends down so they stay folded. Carefully roll the shorter unfolded edge over the burrito, pushing the filling to the back of the roll as you go, to snugly enclose the filling. Keep the 2 ends folded as you roll. Wrap in foil if desired. Repeat with the rest of the tortillas.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Money Breakfast Burritos
raw_recipe.description: Yummy breakfast burritos are stuffed with sausage, scrambled eggs, cheese, and salsa. Bring your breakfast along with you.

review.reviewBody: I am the submitter of this recipe-make sure you use the green chilies in these~~they really make these outstanding!! I prefer mine without cheese. You can defrost them overnight in the fridge.
What is the best way to defrost. Could one defrost over night and heat in oven......I would like to defrost 10-12 at once rather than use microwave.

I scaled back to only make what I needed and wish I had made the entire recipe, but I only had a little sausage, so I adjusted to what I had available. I understand how these could be moneymakers. They are that tasty and so fast and easy to pull together. I minced my onions super tiny so they would cook all the way through and start getting a little golden carmelization color. I just used the same pan for all of this. I heated my tortillas first in the hot dry skillet, then kept them warm while I cooked the sausage and onions. I used roasted chopped Hatch green chilies right from the jar, just a couple spoonfuls, and right into the pan, then the scrambled eggs, and cook and stir as needed, and that Velveeta last. These were very good and I didn't save any for later. I ate what I made right on the spot and it was fantastic. The next time, I will make up a full batch and definitely have these on hand for a hot breakfast before heading out, because this is much better than going by a drive through window or convenience store to grab an early morning bite. I enjoyed every bite of this. I wouldn't leave anything out, it all works so well together, even the Velveeta, which adds a really nice creaminess. I wrap these in foil sheets and they are easy to grab and go for those rushed mornings. I can make these up even on a weekday in around 20 minutes from start to finish. You can't get anything this good from a drive thru window.

I made a couple changes for personal preference but the bones of this recipe were great. I cooked about 2 cups of hash browns first then cooked the sausage and onions and I added one orange pepper just to get it used up. I only scrambled 8 eggs to offset the bulk of the potatoes. Rolled them into tortillas and wrapped in Saran for the freezer. I ran out of tortillas so we had 2 breakfast bowls for lunch. Delicious. Don’t skip the green chiles as they are worth it.
We really enjoyed this recipe! We'll be making our breakfast burritos like this from now on. Thank you!

Very, very good. Made exactly as per the recipe. After all, how can I rate a recipe if I change it? Needs no extra seasoning. I had to scale down to match what I had on hand so I ended up with 6, 5 went in the freezer. I ate one right away and if the submitter’s comment about it tasting better later on is correct, I’m looking forward to more of these. Great idea. Excellent recipe
Very good! We froze them and grabbed them on the go for breakfast. Will make again for sure.
The best breakfast burritos I've made. Simple, wonderful ingredients that make the best tasting dish.

This is a great basic recipe for a quick breakfast. I made it once and it was delicious, but I made some changes the second time. I used chorizo instead of regular pork sausage as I wanted some more spice. I also browned a bag of frozen Potatoes O'Brien threw them into the mix. I added diced green onions to the eggs and doubled the green chiles. Since I was serving this to a young men's soccer team (think 20 hungry 18 year olds) I ended up doubling everything and then threw it into a crock pot on the warm setting. When they were ready to eat, I just loaded up the burritos with filling, salsa, and cheese (did not use processed cheese, but a Mexican blend and Queso Fresco). I ended up with a little left over filling, so just made extra burritos, wrapped them in waxed paper and froze them. They are great to take out of the freezer in the morning, use the defrost setting on the microwave and then finish heating on a regular setting.

These were amazing just the way the recipe was written. My 14 year old son said that was the best breakfast he had in a long time and my husband said a few more good words than that. We will be eating these frequently.
I left out the velveeta (that stuff is expensive to me) and used smokey links in place of the pork sausage. Turned out yummy!

Great for breakfast "on the go"! I cut way back on the serving size because I didn't need that many. I used microwave sausage links that I cut in half lengthwise and then scrambled my eggs and usual adding the green chiles. I didn't have Velveeta on hand so I subbed a Mexican blend and used a fresh salsa. Just about anything you put in a warm tortilla is gonna taste great and this was delicious with a side of light sour cream!
